display.purpose: The masthead title. One per page, never repeated.

headline.purpose: Category titles — the mid-band step between section heads and display.

title.purpose: Card, sheet and panel titles. Fixed at 1.6rem to stay above the 24px large-text grading line.

body.purpose: All prose, capped at the 42rem reading measure. Never fluid.

control.purpose: Tabs, buttons and action pills — a type role in its own right, not a shrunk body size.

label.purpose: Uppercase tracked micro-labels: kickers, credits, and 'Checked [date]' stamps.

shadows.name: rest
shadows.purpose: The barely-there seat under a resting card. Present, not visible.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: A card's response to a pointer, paired with translateY(-2px).

shadows.name: hover-lift-hub
shadows.purpose: The hub grid's larger cards, paired with translateY(-3px).

shadows.name: accent-state-glow
shadows.purpose: Active tab and Today chip. A coloured shadow marks selection, never elevation.

shadows.name: overlay
shadows.purpose: Modals and dialogs — the 'above everything' tier.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Bottom sheets, throwing upward from the screen edge.

shadows.name: focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Inputs and live markers. Offsetless by intent — a ring, not a shadow.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Entries, reveals, panel and tab transitions. Fast start, long settle.

motion.name: ease-spring
motion.purpose: Gentle overshoot for press-release and hover-lift.

motion.name: dur-tap
motion.purpose: Touch feedback. Nothing eases in from stillness on user input.

components.description: The hub hero's single call to action. Ink-filled pill on paper — the only place a solid dark fill is spent.

components.name: Verification stamp + provenance dot
components.description: The signature mark of the product's promise: a dated stamp with an inline dot that opens the source. Sized to the text it annotates, so it reads as a notation rather than a control.

components.name: Status pill (stale)
components.description: Caution ochre, outline-only. Appears solely when a fact has passed its shelf life — an honest mark, not a decoration.

narrative.overview:
Waypoint looks like something that was measured, not something that was described. The governing image is a survey sheet: paper that has been out in the field, carrying contour lines, coordinates, dated marks, and annotations in iron-oxide pigment. Everything that makes the product trustworthy — the source stamp, the verification date, the ≈ on a sourced approximation, the ⚠ on an unconfirmed one — is a survey notation, and the visual system treats those marks as first-class content rather than as fine print to be tucked away.

The system runs on two grounds and one instrument. In daylight it is cool sage survey paper under blue-black map ink. At night it becomes a chart room: a deep slate table under lamplit paper. Neither is a theme in the decorative sense; they are the same document under different light, which is why the guide's identity colour deliberately does not re-map between them. A country's accent is data, not decoration.

Density is deliberately low. A guide has to carry an entire trip while still feeling like something you can read on a phone with one hand. That tension is resolved by restraint rather than compression: surfaces are flat and quiet at rest, hairlines do the separating work, and the accent appears rarely enough that when it does appear, it means something.
keyCharacteristics: Cartographic, not editorial: paper and ink, contour fields, coordinates, dated marks.
One serif doing two jobs through a real optical-size axis; one quiet sans for data.
Flat at rest, hairline-separated; shadow is reserved for state and for stacking order.
Per-country accent as identity data, never re-mapped by theme.
Provenance rendered, not hidden — the stamp is part of the design.

rules.name: The Three Jobs Rule
rules.body: An accent has three jobs and they are three different colours. Identity is --accent. Accent as text is --accent-ink. Text on an accent fill is --on-accent. Never hand-blend a fourth at the call site — a color-mix invented in a rule carries no contrast contract.

rules.name: The Identity Doesn't Theme Rule
rules.body: --accent is the same value in light and dark. Only its ink re-maps. A guide's colour is a fact about the guide, not about the reader's display.

rules.name: The Tinted Ground Rule
rules.body: Accent text is rarely painted on a flat surface — chips and pills tint their ground toward the accent, the one direction that eats contrast. Never tint a background past 18%.

rules.name: The Fluid Headings, Fixed Text Rule
rules.body: The heading band clamps; body and UI text never do. A phone is held closer than a monitor, so reading text wants the same physical size on both.

rules.name: The Rem-In-The-Middle Rule
rules.body: Every clamp's middle term carries a rem component. A pure-vw middle locks size to the viewport and stops responding to the reader's own font-size setting — a WCAG 1.4.4 failure.

rules.name: The 24px Grading Rule
rules.body: Headings are weight 400, which puts their WCAG large-text line at 24px rather than 18.7px. Every heading step stays above it.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest. A shadow appears only as a response to state (hover, focus, drag) or as a signal of stacking order (modal, sheet, popover).

rules.name: The Heavy-Shadow-Means-On-Top Rule
rules.body: The 18px/50px class of shadow is reserved for things that are literally above everything else. Give a card that shadow at rest and modals stop reading as modal.

dos: Do derive accent text from --accent-ink and text-on-accent from --on-accent, always.
Do reach for a token from the type scale — including --text-control and --text-control-sm for anything that is a button, tab, pill, badge, or counter.
Do separate surfaces with a 1px hairline and the tonal ramp before considering a shadow.
Do keep prose inside --read (42rem) and let only maps, galleries, and tables break out.
Do state a verification date wherever a perishable fact appears, in the micro-label role.
Do re-run the axe gate after any change to a colour token — it covers hub and guides across light, dark, desktop, and 375px.
donts: Don't invent an accent shade at a call site with color-mix. That is how a 4.45:1 text colour shipped.
Don't re-map --accent for dark mode. Only its ink re-maps.
Don't tint any background more than 18% toward the accent.
Don't give a resting surface an overlay-weight shadow; that shadow means 'above everything'.
Don't make heading type fluid below 24px, or body and UI type fluid at all.
Don't introduce a second sans, a monospace, or a display face. Three roles, two faces.
Don't use cream paper, full-bleed aspirational photography, or script display type.
Don't reach for the SaaS-dashboard defaults: a blue primary, a uniform card grid as page structure, one neutral sans everywhere, or a gradient CTA.
Don't hard-code --chrome-h, surface hexes, or the light/dark grounds outside base.css.
